name: Bilastine
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Bilastine is a non-sedating antihistamine that is not metabolized; about 28% is excreted unchanged in urine. Exposure rises about 2.3-fold in severe kidney impairment, but the European label needs no dose change in adults. It advises avoiding P-glycoprotein inhibitors (such as ketoconazole, erythromycin, cyclosporine, ritonavir, diltiazem) in moderate or severe kidney impairment. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: SmPC pharmacokinetic groups use glomerular filtration rate (GFR, mL/min/1.73 m2); no dose adjustment at any level. Bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 20 mg once daily, 1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juice (SmPC).

hd: Not studied in dialysis (SmPC silent). No adjustment in severe impairment; avoid P-glycoprotein inhibitors.
monitoring: QT risk factors (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia, bradycardia, QT-prolonging drugs) (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: 2 years and older, weighing at least 15 kg (SmPC).
pediatric.usual_dose: 2 to 11 years (15 kg or more): 10 mg once daily (orodispersible tablet or oral solution). 12 years and older: 20 mg once daily.
